To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) TCS was eliminated in primary sedimentation, 2) TCS was biodegraded during wastewater treatment, 3) 2,4-DCP and 2, 8-DCDD were formed in the presence of chlorine, and 4) MTCS was formed during aerobic sludge digestion.
TCS is susceptible to transformation during wastewater/sludge treatment processes.
TCS was adsorbable and biotransformable in the studied wastewater/sludge treatment systems and its elimination efficiency was strongly correlated to the loading concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate of TCS in three wastewater treatment plants and its transformation to degradation products.
the fate of TCS in wastewater and sewage treatment plants and the probability of transformation of TCS into other compounds.
the fate of TCS during wastewater treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elimination of TCS in wastewater/sludge treatment is governed by a number of factors including loading concentration, type of treatment, and type of sludge digestion.
TCS is a persistent compound and is not completely removed in the wastewater treatment plants.
TCS is a susceptible compound to biodegradation and chemical transformation in the wastewater treatment processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TCS was not readily eliminated in primary sedimentation, and the elimination efficiency was directly correlated to loading concentration.
TCS and its degradation products were not completely eliminated in the studied processes.
TCS was susceptible to degradation and transformation processes in the investigated treatment practices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TCS is not only a recalcitrant compound, but also it is a potential source of toxic/persistent degradation products.
the TCS degradation in primary sedimentation was mainly attributed to the adsorption to the sludge.
TCS and its degradation products are susceptible to transformation/degradation during the treatment of wastewater and sewage sludges.
